# TypeScript best practices

On Muse, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/muse-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

Apply the **type-system-discipline** principle skill first.

| Rule | Summary |
|------|---------|
| Discriminated unions | Model variants with a `kind` literal discriminant so impossible states can't be represented. No optional-field bags. |
| Branded types | Brand primitives with `& { readonly __brand: "X" }` so they can't be mixed up. Validate once at the boundary. A brand comes from a verifying type guard (`input is AgentId`), never from `as`. |
| Constructive modeling | Build the shape so the illegal value can't be constructed. `[T, ...T[]]` for non-empty, `[T, T][]` for even length, `start` plus `duration` for a range. Not a runtime guard, not a wish for refinement types. |
| Simplest total type | Keep `T[]` while every operation on it stays total. Strengthen to `NonEmpty<T>` only where the loose type forces `!`, a cast, or a "should never happen" throw. |
| `unknown` over `any` | External data is `unknown`. |
| Schemas before guards | Before hand-writing a property-by-property type guard, use the repository's runtime schema library and infer the type from the schema, such as `z.infer`. |
| No `as` casts | Every `as` is a runtime crash waiting. Cast only after validation. |
| Narrowing hierarchy | Discriminant switch > `in` operator > `typeof`/`instanceof` > user-defined type guard > `as`. |
| Type guards | Must verify the claim. A lying guard is worse than `as` because the bug hides behind a name that says it's safe. Name them `isX` or `hasX`. |
| Exhaustiveness | Inline `const _exhaustive: never = x;` in default arms so the compiler errors when a new variant is added. |
| `satisfies` over `as` | Validates the value without widening literal types. |
| Boundary validation | Parse where data crosses in, into a named domain type. `Record<string, unknown>` (however spelled) stops at that parse. Trust types inside. See the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. |
| Schema-derived types | Reach for `Pick`/`Omit`/`Parameters`/`ReturnType`/`Awaited`/`typeof` before declaring a new interface. |
| Object args | Pass objects, not positional, so argument order is self-documenting. Skip on hot paths (per-frame render, tokenizers, parsers). |
| Real tests | Don't mock what you can run. Prefer the framework's real test primitives with leak/disposable checks, and verify UI in a running build. Mock only what you can't run locally. |
| Structured telemetry | Prefer structured logger diagnostics with enough context to debug from an id. No `console.log` in shipped code. |

Examples: `references/patterns.md`.
# Exposed UI

Import components and public types from the `src/lib/ui/index.ts` barrel (for example `./lib/ui` from `src/Example.svelte`). Load `../lib/ui/styles.css` once in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. It includes tokens, actions, patterns, focus rings, hidden captions, highlighted text and animation prerequisites. Field and Notice keep scoped styles. `/design-system` is the interactive reference in development only and requires no declarations API. Production returns 404 and hides its footer link.

Features own amounts, availability, chart geometry, URLs, analytics and async work. UI accepts formatted strings and presentation models. Pages own grids and section spacing. Use the [composition recipes](COMPOSITION.md) for native rows, declarations and identities.

| Component                              | Contract                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Button, ButtonLink                     | `variant` primary/secondary/quiet/subtle; `size` regular/large/compact/inline. Native attributes and handlers pass through. Button defaults to `type="button"`; links require `href`.                                                |
| Field                                  | Required visible `label`; `type` text/search/date; bindable string `value`; `defaultValue` supports native reset. `hint` and `error` join caller `aria-describedby`. Native attributes reach the input; `class` reaches the wrapper. |
| SearchField                            | Required `label`, `help` snippet and `onclear`; bindable string `value` and native `input` reference; optional `shortcut`. Native attributes including `class` reach the input. Caller owns query behavior and focus restoration.    |
| Notice                                 | `tone` neutral/accent/warning. Native div attributes pass through. Caller chooses announcement `role`.                                                                                                                               |
| Badge                                  | `variant` result (default), profile or legend. `class` adds a root hook without replacing appearance.                                                                                                                                |
| MessageState                           | Required `title`; `variant` centered (default) or detail; `level` 1/2 changes semantics independently of appearance. Optional `icon`, `children`, `actions`, `role`, additive root `class`.                                          |
| SectionHeading                         | Required `id`, `title`; optional `level` 1/2/3 and trailing children. Heading presentation stays independent of rank.                                                                                                                |
| Disclosure                             | Required `summary`, children; `variant` names (default) or plain. Native details attributes, additive root `class`, bindable `open`.                                                                                                 |
| Metric                                 | Required `label`, formatted `value`; optional `regionLabel`, `available`, `description`, `level` 2/3. `variant` default or expanded; optional `align` start/end overrides variant and responsive text alignment. Available values remain keyboard-scrollable regions; unavailable text remains ordinary text.    |
| DeclarationCard                        | Required `heading`, `registered`, children snippets. `variant` default or compact changes padding.                                                                                                                                   |
| ValueRow                               | Required `source` and `value` snippets. Owns its `li` layout, including outside `.funding-list`; nested lists retain native layout.                                                                                                  |
| DataTable                              | Required text `caption`, `head` snippet and body children. Callers supply native rows, cells, scope and column-specific classes. No numeric alignment or column widths are assumed.                                                  |
| IdentityHeader                         | Required `name`, `kind`, `metadata`; optional `values`, `navigation`, `level` 1/2/3.                                                                                                                                                 |
| ResultRow, DeclarationList             | Native `li` and `ol` wrappers; children and optional accessible `label`. ResultRow callers supply their own anchor and may add a root `class` for a local palette.                                                                   |
| SignedBarList                          | `bars: SignedBar[]`, `baseline`; `variant` default or compact. Values are formatted strings; widths and signs come from features.                                                                                                    |
| BarChart, PieChart                     | Typed `ChartBar[]` geometry and `PieSlice[]` presentation data. Features calculate shares, signs and totals. See [RegistrationTimeline](../../RegistrationTimeline.svelte) and [FunderSummary](../../FunderSummary.svelte).          |
| ViewLinks, ViewLink, Pagination        | Native navigation. Callers own destinations/current page; Pagination owns bound availability.                                                                                                                                        |
| Icon, IconIndicator                    | Canonical `IconName`; Icon is decorative. IconIndicator owns focus, pointer and Escape hints.                                                                                                                                        |
| HighlightedText, Spinner, SkeletonRows | Literal text highlights and decorative progress.                                                                                                                                                                                     |

The first DataTable body row has a top divider, including when callers visually hide column headings.

Classes on native-attribute components accept Svelte class arrays and objects. Where a structural component exposes `class`, it adds a root hook. No class replacement API is supported. Use finite variants for existing appearances; caller-authored snippet classes own feature text and arrangements. The recipes show those classes explicitly.

Tokens in [tokens.css](tokens.css) own colors, spacing, type and focus. Override `--accent` on a container for another palette, such as `var(--accent-funder)`. The Exposed wordmark stays white across entity contexts. The landing heading uses member purple for MPs and funder teal for financial interests. Entity indicators, badges, highlights, charts and declared values derive their colors from the local accent; a ResultRow root `class` can select that palette explicitly. Actions use neutral `--action`, `--action-ink`, `--action-border`, `--action-surface` and `--action-hover`; all focus rings use `--focus-color`, independently of entity palettes. Keep action and focus tokens neutral in member and funder containers. `--focus-width` and `--focus-offset` apply at the root or on a container. Native links, buttons and summaries add one pixel to the offset. Do not import internal stylesheets individually.

The [barrel](index.ts) is the public inventory. The gallery covers native disclosure/input behavior, precise metric overflow, repeated association IDs and pointer tooltip lifecycle. Financial parsing and availability decisions belong in feature adapters, never in UI components.

UI-owned snippet classes are `.results-list` (list reset and divider), `.entity-text` (shrinkable content), `.entity-name` (result anchor typography and hover), `.entity-alias` (secondary result text), `.funding-list` (nested list reset and spacing), `.declaration-reference`, `.payment-type`, `.currency-label`, `.empty-entry` (declaration context), `.amount` (exact value typography), and `.entry-count`/`.partial-note` (secondary chart/table text). These work with the single UI stylesheet import. Feature grids and custom table columns stay in callers.

`CategoryWheel` accepts `CategoryWheelOption[]` with caller-owned closed SVG sector `path`, open outer-boundary `rimPath` in the same local coordinates, and label positions, a selected identity, accessible group `label`, optional pixel `size` (default 284), and `onselect`. Native pressed buttons cover the complete sectors. Muted category surfaces, icons, labels and fine inner/radial boundaries stay constant. Selection brightens only the outer rim; focus uses a neutral full-sector outline. A decorative neutral chart glyph occupies the center. Features provide a size that fits the layout.

`RankingList` accepts formatted `RankingRow[]` and an accessible list `label`. Features supply stable keys, destinations, amounts, coverage, signs and bar widths. The list animates row and bar entry and disables animation for reduced motion. Party identities can omit destinations.
# Composition recipes

Each example is a complete Svelte component placed at `src/Example.svelte`. Load `../lib/ui/styles.css` once in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. These examples use static presentation data; production features supply real URLs and formatted values.

Actions and focus remain neutral in every entity context. Override `--accent` only for entity meaning, such as funder badges, highlights and charts.

# Monthly updates design

Use /tmp/monthly-design-astra.md as the base sketch. All three candidates recommend a dedicated updates service and nonfinancial repository projection. The service exposes one current-month operation; RegistrationMonth owns UTC half-open boundaries. Query one snapshot across every category, canonicalize funders, retain no-entry MPs, deduplicate declaration IDs per entity, return all rows ordered latest registration descending then exact name then ID. Share exhaustive FunderKind::is_individual with rankings. Keep financial totals unchanged.

Frontend /updates uses a server-only parser and SSR load. Show Updates, formatted UTC month, MPs and Companies sections, entity profile links, declaration counts and latest dates. Reuse ResultRow and existing tokens. Add a landing-page Updates link, no new explanatory copy. No amounts, pagination, or month picker.

The nonzero EntityUpdate count from Astra prevents an empty entity row. Keep optional member party/constituency context out of this first view to reduce copy and query payload. HTTP captures one UTC clock instant and passes it into UpdatesService::updates(now); service constructs the typed month. Tests supply an explicit instant.

Rejected extending RankingsService because it couples activity with financial ranking rules. Rejected SQL aggregation because it duplicates classification and hides count policy from domain tests.

Rubric scores by parent, completeness/invariants/interface/isolation/testability. Astra 5/5/5/5/5. Sol 5/5/4/5/5. Luna 5/4/5/5/4. All designs converge; Astra gives the clearest exact ordering and nonzero shape. Cross-judge agrees Astra base, scoring Astra 25, Sol 24, Luna 21. Adopt Sol explicit service instant supplied once by HTTP for deterministic full-service tests, replacing current_month() with updates(now). Also validate month boundaries and row membership in frontend parser. Parent accepts both grafts.
# Monthly updates: dedicated activity projection

## Problem and grounding

`rankings` has useful integration patterns but the wrong data contract for updates. Its service loads declarations since the parliament boundary, applies exact financial totals, limits every board to ten, and includes funders only for DonationSupport. Its repository selects all financial entry columns and parses currencies and categories into `MemberDeclaration`; canonical identity comes from `funder_alias_groups`, root `funders`, and `funder_group_names`. Its HTTP adapter formats identities; the frontend server parser enforces ten entries and a financial total. Reusing that operation would silently lose relevant records or import irrelevant financial validation. `AppState<E,D,R>` currently injects three services. The Svelte route uses a server load, private API origin, typed page data, and AppShell. AppShell has no primary navigation; its footer contains Methodology and development-only Design system. Updates should integrate through the same server-load pattern and an Updates navigation link without reworking the shell.

## Usage (written before types)

Backend HTTP handler:
```rust
let updates = state.updates_service.current_month().await?;
Ok(ApiSuccess::new(StatusCode::OK, UpdatesResponse::from(updates)))
```
Frontend server load:
```ts
return { updates: await loadUpdates(fetch, request.signal, origin), error: null };
// Catch maps to existing-style user-facing error; no client API origin.
```
Page:
```svelte
<AppShell target="updates" current="updates">
  <main id="updates" tabindex="-1">
    <h1>Updates</h1>
    <!-- backend month formatted with timeZone: UTC -->
    <!-- MPs and Companies sections, existing ResultRow composition -->
    <!-- native profile anchor, declaration count, latest registration date -->
  </main>
</AppShell>
```
Each returned section contains every qualifying identity, in final display order. Callers do not select a month, apply a cutoff, classify funders, deduplicate, sort, paginate, calculate totals, or join data.

## Shape

Choose a dedicated `updates` model, repository projection, and application service. Keep existing rankings public API unchanged. Reuse canonical identity resolution SQL join shape and the existing MemberId, FunderId and FunderKind types, not ranking financial objects. The interface is one operation that hides calendar selection, scope, canonicalization, distinct counting and ordering.

```rust
// domain/models/updates.rs
pub struct RegistrationMonth { start: DateTime<Utc>, end: DateTime<Utc> }
impl RegistrationMonth {
    // Private fields; start is UTC day 1 midnight, end the following month's start.
    pub fn containing(now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Self { todo!() }
    pub fn start(&self) -> DateTime<Utc> { todo!() }
    pub fn end(&self) -> DateTime<Utc> { todo!() }
}
pub struct UpdatedMember { pub id: MemberId, pub name: String }
pub struct UpdatedCompany { pub id: FunderId, pub name: String }
pub struct EntityUpdate<I> {
    pub identity: I,
    pub declaration_count: NonZeroUsize,
    pub latest_registration: DateTime<Utc>,
}
pub struct MonthlyUpdates {
    pub month: RegistrationMonth,
    pub members: Vec<EntityUpdate<UpdatedMember>>,
    pub companies: Vec<EntityUpdate<UpdatedCompany>>,
}
// Repository-facing domain facts, not wire or database rows.
pub struct UpdateDeclaration {
    pub source_id: i32,
    pub registered_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub member: UpdatedMember,
    pub funders: Vec<UpdateFunder>,
}
pub struct UpdateFunder { pub id: FunderId, pub name: String, pub kind: FunderKind }

// domain/repositories/updates.rs
pub trait UpdatesRepo: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn declarations(&self, month: &RegistrationMonth)
        -> impl Future<Output = Result<Vec<UpdateDeclaration>, UpdatesError>> + Send;
}
// domain/services/updates.rs
pub trait UpdatesService: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn current_month(&self)
        -> impl Future<Output = Result<MonthlyUpdates, UpdatesError>> + Send;
}
pub struct Service<R> { repo: R }
impl<R: UpdatesRepo> Service<R> {
    pub fn new(repo: R) -> Self { todo!() }
    // Service samples Utc::now() once and derives one month before fetching.
    // Pure summarization is independently testable with a supplied month and facts.
}
fn summarize(month: RegistrationMonth, declarations: Vec<UpdateDeclaration>)
    -> MonthlyUpdates { todo!() }
```
Do not create a shared generic identity abstraction merely to remove two small names-plus-ID structs. Member and funder IDs remain distinct internally; HTTP alone serializes them as strings.

`outbound/updates.rs` implements the repository with one `sqlx::query!` statement: declarations JOIN members, LEFT JOIN funding_entries, LEFT JOIN funder_alias_groups, LEFT JOIN canonical root funders, LEFT JOIN funder_group_names. Select only declaration ID, registration date, member identity, canonical funder ID/name/kind. Filter `d.registration_date >= $1 AND d.registration_date < $2`; no category predicate, no amount/currency predicates, no LIMIT. Preserve declaration rows with no funding entries or no identified funder, because their MP still qualifies. Reconstruct one fact per declaration using stable source-ID ordering. Parse stored FunderKind through its canonical parser; unknown classification is NotSpecified only when absent, matching existing rankings behavior. Malformed nonempty values remain errors.

Add `FunderKind::is_individual()` with an exhaustive match. Both rankings and updates use this method to distinguish individual from all other kinds. This makes the existing companies convention have one owner without inventing a second enum or a synchronized string allowlist. The method's name describes classification rather than incorrectly declaring every organization legally a company. Replace only rankings' classification branch, preserving financial semantics.

`inbound/http/handlers/updates.rs` defines transport-only `UpdatesResponse`: `month_start`, `month_end`, `members`, `companies`; each row has `id`, `name`, `declaration_count`, `latest_registration`. Map nonzero domain count to JSON integer. Add `U: UpdatesService` and `updates_service: Arc<U>` to AppState and route wiring, following the existing explicit dependency pattern. This costs generic-parameter propagation but avoids coupling updates availability to a rankings service.

Frontend `lib/server/updates.ts` owns response parsing and fetch timeout; `lib/updates.ts` owns serializable page models and display formatting; `routes/updates/+page.server.ts` owns initial server fetch; `routes/updates/+page.svelte` owns arrangement. Parser validates timestamp shape, IDs, positive safe integer counts and unique identities within each section. It accepts arrays longer than ten. Preserve backend order. No financial helpers or decimal conversion are needed. Display dates using UTC and use existing `/members/{id}` and `/funders/{canonical-id}` destinations. Reuse ResultRow, SectionHeading and Notice; native lists and feature-authored counts/date content need no new shared component. Add only Updates, month, MPs, Companies, counts, dates, required error/empty wording and navigation text; no explanatory subtitles or badges.

## Ownership and exact rules

RegistrationMonth alone owns UTC calendar arithmetic, including December rollover and leap years. Current month is sampled once per request on the backend and sent to the frontend; browser time zones and import timestamps cannot change membership. Start is inclusive, next month start exclusive; null registration dates never qualify. Future-dated records within the current month qualify, because the rule is month membership rather than month-to-now. All source category IDs qualify, including unknown IDs. Amounts, currency, missing amounts and payment types do not influence this feature.

Repository owns storage mapping and canonical aliases. Canonical root determines ID and kind, preferred group name determines display name, root name is fallback. Service owns activity aggregation and ordering. Track source declaration IDs per entity to count each source declaration once. Multiple funding entries, repeated occurrences and aliases resolving to one canonical group contribute one count to that company. One declaration involving several companies contributes once to each. Members count declarations even without a company. Individual canonical roots are excluded only from Companies, never from their recipient MP's activity.

After grouping, sort each section by latest registration descending, then exact stored display name ascending, then numeric MemberId or UUID bytes ascending. Use Rust ordering to avoid database collation/environment differences. All identities are retained. EntityUpdate uses a nonzero count and nonoptional date because rows cannot exist without at least one qualifying declaration. No ranking, financial total or coverage state is exposed.

## Alternatives considered

1. Extend RankingsService with updates and reuse ranking_declarations(start). This is initially fewer files but exposes unrelated capabilities through one service, loads financial values, lacks an upper SQL cutoff, and invites reuse of category filtering or top-ten truncation. Its apparent small surface hides two incoherent operations. Reject.
2. Rename the existing fact repository to declaration activity and have both services reuse a rich financial declaration stream with optional end bound. This avoids duplicate canonical joins but forces updates to understand and parse amounts, currencies and categories; it changes ranking persistence solely for a second consumer and introduces a generic range absent a real need. Reject for this feature.
3. SQL-aggregate complete update results and use a forwarding service. This makes the repository deep and reduces memory, but places company vocabulary and sorting rules inside SQL or exposes internal classification groups; separate member/company queries also risk inconsistent snapshots without a transaction. A single lightweight fact query with pure service aggregation fits this project's domain ownership better.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- Accept one duplicated canonical join shape in exchange for an independently meaningful minimal read projection; canonical schema tables remain the source of truth, and alias fixture coverage protects semantics.
- Accept a fourth AppState parameter in exchange for explicit service ownership and isolated tests. Do not introduce a broader dependency injection refactor in this feature.
- Accept memory proportional to current-month declaration facts in exchange for a single consistent statement snapshot and clear distinct-count rules. No pagination can silently reduce the promised list.

## Test plan

Pure month tests: ordinary month, UTC offset converted across month boundary, December rollover, leap February. Pure aggregation tests: start included, just before excluded, end excluded, missing dates excluded at repository boundary; same declaration repeated, multiple entries and alias occurrences counted once; multiple companies per declaration; unknown category and no-entry MP retained; canonical Individual excluded while every other enum kind included; stable ties by name and ID; more than ten identities retained; empty month.

SQLx fixture integration: root/alias mappings with preferred name, conflicting alias-vs-root kinds (root wins), declarations with no entries, null dates, boundary timestamps, duplicate canonical occurrences, multiple categories. Assert the projection carries no financial dependency and one statement returns both entity families consistently. Service tests assert counts and ordering through the returned domain model.

Frontend parser tests: more than ten rows, malformed IDs/dates/counts, duplicates, exact field mapping, empty arrays and API failure. Playwright: SSR initial content, Updates navigation/current indication, both sections and correct existing-profile links, UTC month display, newest-first rows, no currency/financial amount column, empty/error states. Run repository verify requirements, npm check/build and affected Playwright; capture desktop screenshot for PR attachment.

## Red-flag screen

One public operation per service; no caller-orchestrated pipeline. No wire types in domain, no new transport reuse, no generic financial options, no extra optional states, no mutable cache, no duplicated finite vocabulary, no multiple update-loading APIs. Separate repository is a real persistence boundary; service adds calendar and aggregation policy rather than passing through.

## Synthesis decision

Candidate for orchestration comparison; no claim to synthesize other runners.

## Implementation reconciliation

No implementation performed. Root should reconcile final accepted shape before delegating implementation.

## Open questions and risks

No user decision required for this scoped design. If the current-month volume proves materially large, should a later measured optimization aggregate distinct declarations in SQL while retaining canonical classification ownership? That is deferred, not a blocker.

## Next implementation step

Build RegistrationMonth and activity projection fixtures, then implement the minimal query and pure summary against their boundary and alias-count contracts.

# Rust domain development

Apply the [repository coding policy](../../../AGENTS.md). Choose the representation
that enforces the required behavior before adding implementation logic.

## Find the owner

Name the incoming data shape, the valid domain states, and the invariant the
change must preserve. Find the existing type that owns that rule. Search its
callers and serialized spellings before creating another representation.

Trace a changed domain type through its producer, encoder, decoder, service,
and persistence mapping. Change the affected consumers in the same task.

## Choose the representation

- Use an enum for a closed vocabulary. Share its serialization and deserialization
  definition across producers and consumers. When a separately versioned external
  contract needs its own type, convert it explicitly into the canonical domain
  type at the boundary.
- Represent mutually exclusive states with an enum carrying the fields each
  state requires. Use newtypes for identifiers with different meanings and
  checked constructors for values whose validity depends on runtime facts.
- Use exhaustive matches without a fallback when variants require different
  behavior. Adding a variant must require a decision at those matches. Do not
  add artificial matches when every variant already supports the same operation.
- Keep transport DTOs only where the external shape differs from the domain
  shape. Their domain-bearing fields still use the canonical types. Reuse an
  existing result record when it already defines the serialized contract.

## Parse at the boundary

Decode external values into domain types before passing them to services.
Reject unknown labels during parsing. Do not parse a domain enum into a string
and then reconstruct its vocabulary with a membership check.

Keep checks for runtime facts such as duplicate IDs, missing references,
artifact digests, and stored timestamps at the responsible boundary. Types
cannot establish facts about files or database rows that have not been read.
Propagate the existing error types instead of hiding failures with defaults.

Keep domain decisions in the domain model and transaction ownership in the
repository. Convert typed values into storage representations at the persistence
boundary using the canonical encoding. Preserve existing service abstractions.

## Fix the structure

When a failure reveals two owners for one rule, identify the canonical owner and
delete the competing definition. Updating both copies leaves the cause intact.
Stay within the affected contract rather than expanding into unrelated cleanup.

In Exposed, the resolution domain owns `IdentityBasis`, `PairReason`, and the
attribution decision types in
[`declaration_resolution.rs`](../../../exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution.rs).
The [declaration loader](../../../exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs)
must decode those types. It must not maintain a second list of accepted labels.
This applies to other finite domain vocabularies too.

## Verify the contract

Run the relevant behavior checks and the real entry point affected by the change.
For serialized contracts, verify that producer output is readable by the consumer
and that malformed external values are rejected. Preserve the intended wire
format, supported versions, and persistence behavior unless the task changes them.

Check the compiler guarantee directly when the task relies on it. For example,
temporarily add a variant to confirm the semantic matches reject missing handling,
then revert the probe. A passing runtime test does not prove exhaustiveness.

Run formatting and applicable compiler or lint checks. Distinguish diagnostics
introduced by the change from existing failures. Report which invalid state the
types now exclude and which runtime checks remain necessary.

On Claude Code they work as written. On Codex, read [`references/codex-tools.md`](references/codex-tools.md) for the Codex equivalent of a Claude tool, model, or skill named by these workflows. On Pi, read [`references/pi-tools.md`](references/pi-tools.md) instead. On GitHub Copilot, CLI or app, read [`references/copilot-tools.md`](references/copilot-tools.md) instead. # Monthly updates: dedicated activity projection

## Problem and grounding

`rankings` has useful integration patterns but the wrong data contract for updates. Its service loads declarations since the parliament boundary, applies exact financial totals, limits every board to ten, and includes funders only for DonationSupport. Its repository selects all financial entry columns and parses currencies and categories into `MemberDeclaration`; canonical identity comes from `funder_alias_groups`, root `funders`, and `funder_group_names`. Its HTTP adapter formats identities; the frontend server parser enforces ten entries and a financial total. Reusing that operation would silently lose relevant records or import irrelevant financial validation. `AppState<E,D,R>` currently injects three services. The Svelte route uses a server load, private API origin, typed page data, and AppShell. AppShell has no primary navigation; its footer contains Methodology and development-only Design system. Updates should integrate through the same server-load pattern and an Updates navigation link without reworking the shell.

## Usage (written before types)

Backend HTTP handler:
```rust
let updates = state.updates_service.current_month().await?;
Ok(ApiSuccess::new(StatusCode::OK, UpdatesResponse::from(updates)))
```
Frontend server load:
```ts
return { updates: await loadUpdates(fetch, request.signal, origin), error: null };
// Catch maps to existing-style user-facing error; no client API origin.
```
Page:
```svelte
<AppShell target="updates" current="updates">
  <main id="updates" tabindex="-1">
    <h1>Updates</h1>
    <!-- backend month formatted with timeZone: UTC -->
    <!-- MPs and Companies sections, existing ResultRow composition -->
    <!-- native profile anchor, declaration count, latest registration date -->
  </main>
</AppShell>
```
Each returned section contains every qualifying identity, in final display order. Callers do not select a month, apply a cutoff, classify funders, deduplicate, sort, paginate, calculate totals, or join data.

## Shape

Choose a dedicated `updates` model, repository projection, and application service. Keep existing rankings public API unchanged. Reuse canonical identity resolution SQL join shape and the existing MemberId, FunderId and FunderKind types, not ranking financial objects. The interface is one operation that hides calendar selection, scope, canonicalization, distinct counting and ordering.

```rust
impl RegistrationMonth {
    // Private fields; start is UTC day 1 midnight, end the following month's start.
    pub fn containing(now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Self { todo!() }
    pub fn start(&self) -> DateTime<Utc> { todo!() }
    pub fn end(&self) -> DateTime<Utc> { todo!() }
}
pub struct UpdatedMember { pub id: MemberId, pub name: String }
pub struct UpdatedCompany { pub id: FunderId, pub name: String }
pub struct EntityUpdate<I> {
    pub identity: I,
    pub declaration_count: NonZeroUsize,
    pub latest_registration: DateTime<Utc>,
}
pub struct MonthlyUpdates {
    pub month: RegistrationMonth,
    pub members: Vec<EntityUpdate<UpdatedMember>>,
    pub companies: Vec<EntityUpdate<UpdatedCompany>>,
}
// Repository-facing domain facts, not wire or database rows.
pub struct UpdateDeclaration {
    pub source_id: i32,
    pub registered_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub member: UpdatedMember,
    pub funders: Vec<UpdateFunder>,
}
pub struct UpdateFunder { pub id: FunderId, pub name: String, pub kind: FunderKind }

// domain/repositories/updates.rs
pub trait UpdatesRepo: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn declarations(&self, month: &RegistrationMonth)
        -> impl Future<Output = Result<Vec<UpdateDeclaration>, UpdatesError>> + Send;
}
// domain/services/updates.rs
pub trait UpdatesService: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn current_month(&self)
        -> impl Future<Output = Result<MonthlyUpdates, UpdatesError>> + Send;
}
pub struct Service<R> { repo: R }
impl<R: UpdatesRepo> Service<R> {
    pub fn new(repo: R) -> Self { todo!() }
    // Service samples Utc::now() once and derives one month before fetching.
    // Pure summarization is independently testable with a supplied month and facts.
}
fn summarize(month: RegistrationMonth, declarations: Vec<UpdateDeclaration>)

```
Do not create a shared generic identity abstraction merely to remove two small names-plus-ID structs. Member and funder IDs remain distinct internally; HTTP alone serializes them as strings.

`outbound/updates.rs` implements the repository with one `sqlx::query!` statement: declarations JOIN members, LEFT JOIN funding_entries, LEFT JOIN funder_alias_groups, LEFT JOIN canonical root funders, LEFT JOIN funder_group_names. Select only declaration ID, registration date, member identity, canonical funder ID/name/kind. Filter `d.registration_date >= $1 AND d.registration_date < $2`; no category predicate, no amount/currency predicates, no LIMIT. Preserve declaration rows with no funding entries or no identified funder, because their MP still qualifies. Reconstruct one fact per declaration using stable source-ID ordering. Parse stored FunderKind through its canonical parser; unknown classification is NotSpecified only when absent, matching existing rankings behavior. Malformed nonempty values remain errors.

Add `FunderKind::is_individual()` with an exhaustive match. Both rankings and updates use this method to distinguish individual from all other kinds. This makes the existing companies convention have one owner without inventing a second enum or a synchronized string allowlist. The method's name describes classification rather than incorrectly declaring every organization legally a company. Replace only rankings' classification branch, preserving financial semantics.

`inbound/http/handlers/updates.rs` defines transport-only `UpdatesResponse`: `month_start`, `month_end`, `members`, `companies`; each row has `id`, `name`, `declaration_count`, `latest_registration`. Map nonzero domain count to JSON integer. Add `U: UpdatesService` and `updates_service: Arc<U>` to AppState and route wiring, following the existing explicit dependency pattern. This costs generic-parameter propagation but avoids coupling updates availability to a rankings service.

Frontend `lib/server/updates.ts` owns response parsing and fetch timeout; `lib/updates.ts` owns serializable page models and display formatting; `routes/updates/+page.server.ts` owns initial server fetch; `routes/updates/+page.svelte` owns arrangement. Parser validates timestamp shape, IDs, positive safe integer counts and unique identities within each section. It accepts arrays longer than ten. Preserve backend order. No financial helpers or decimal conversion are needed. Display dates using UTC and use existing `/members/{id}` and `/funders/{canonical-id}` destinations. Reuse ResultRow, SectionHeading and Notice; native lists and feature-authored counts/date content need no new shared component. Add only Updates, month, MPs, Companies, counts, dates, required error/empty wording and navigation text; no explanatory subtitles or badges.

## Ownership and exact rules

RegistrationMonth alone owns UTC calendar arithmetic, including December rollover and leap years. Current month is sampled once per request on the backend and sent to the frontend; browser time zones and import timestamps cannot change membership. Start is inclusive, next month start exclusive; null registration dates never qualify. Future-dated records within the current month qualify, because the rule is month membership rather than month-to-now. All source category IDs qualify, including unknown IDs. Amounts, currency, missing amounts and payment types do not influence this feature.

Repository owns storage mapping and canonical aliases. Canonical root determines ID and kind, preferred group name determines display name, root name is fallback. Service owns activity aggregation and ordering. Track source declaration IDs per entity to count each source declaration once. Multiple funding entries, repeated occurrences and aliases resolving to one canonical group contribute one count to that company. One declaration involving several companies contributes once to each. Members count declarations even without a company. Individual canonical roots are excluded only from Companies, never from their recipient MP's activity.

After grouping, sort each section by latest registration descending, then exact stored display name ascending, then numeric MemberId or UUID bytes ascending. Use Rust ordering to avoid database collation/environment differences. All identities are retained. EntityUpdate uses a nonzero count and nonoptional date because rows cannot exist without at least one qualifying declaration. No ranking, financial total or coverage state is exposed.

## Alternatives considered

1. Extend RankingsService with updates and reuse ranking_declarations(start). This is initially fewer files but exposes unrelated capabilities through one service, loads financial values, lacks an upper SQL cutoff, and invites reuse of category filtering or top-ten truncation. Its apparent small surface hides two incoherent operations. Reject.
2. Rename the existing fact repository to declaration activity and have both services reuse a rich financial declaration stream with optional end bound. This avoids duplicate canonical joins but forces updates to understand and parse amounts, currencies and categories; it changes ranking persistence solely for a second consumer and introduces a generic range absent a real need. Reject for this feature.
3. SQL-aggregate complete update results and use a forwarding service. This makes the repository deep and reduces memory, but places company vocabulary and sorting rules inside SQL or exposes internal classification groups; separate member/company queries also risk inconsistent snapshots without a transaction. A single lightweight fact query with pure service aggregation fits this project's domain ownership better.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- Accept one duplicated canonical join shape in exchange for an independently meaningful minimal read projection; canonical schema tables remain the source of truth, and alias fixture coverage protects semantics.
- Accept a fourth AppState parameter in exchange for explicit service ownership and isolated tests. Do not introduce a broader dependency injection refactor in this feature.
- Accept memory proportional to current-month declaration facts in exchange for a single consistent statement snapshot and clear distinct-count rules. No pagination can silently reduce the promised list.

## Test plan

Pure month tests: ordinary month, UTC offset converted across month boundary, December rollover, leap February. Pure aggregation tests: start included, just before excluded, end excluded, missing dates excluded at repository boundary; same declaration repeated, multiple entries and alias occurrences counted once; multiple companies per declaration; unknown category and no-entry MP retained; canonical Individual excluded while every other enum kind included; stable ties by name and ID; more than ten identities retained; empty month.

SQLx fixture integration: root/alias mappings with preferred name, conflicting alias-vs-root kinds (root wins), declarations with no entries, null dates, boundary timestamps, duplicate canonical occurrences, multiple categories. Assert the projection carries no financial dependency and one statement returns both entity families consistently. Service tests assert counts and ordering through the returned domain model.

Frontend parser tests: more than ten rows, malformed IDs/dates/counts, duplicates, exact field mapping, empty arrays and API failure. Playwright: SSR initial content, Updates navigation/current indication, both sections and correct existing-profile links, UTC month display, newest-first rows, no currency/financial amount column, empty/error states. Run repository verify requirements, npm check/build and affected Playwright; capture desktop screenshot for PR attachment.

## Red-flag screen

One public operation per service; no caller-orchestrated pipeline. No wire types in domain, no new transport reuse, no generic financial options, no extra optional states, no mutable cache, no duplicated finite vocabulary, no multiple update-loading APIs. Separate repository is a real persistence boundary; service adds calendar and aggregation policy rather than passing through.

## Synthesis decision

Candidate for orchestration comparison; no claim to synthesize other runners.

## Implementation reconciliation

No implementation performed. Root should reconcile final accepted shape before delegating implementation.

## Open questions and risks

No user decision required for this scoped design. If the current-month volume proves materially large, should a later measured optimization aggregate distinct declarations in SQL while retaining canonical classification ownership? That is deferred, not a blocker.

## Next implementation step

Build RegistrationMonth and activity projection fixtures, then implement the minimal query and pure summary against their boundary and alias-count contracts.

Read the leaf skill in full for any principle you apply. Each entry names when it applies. Each leaf is the **principle-<title>** skill, with the title in kebab case, hyphens kept and other punctuation dropped, unless the entry gives its name.

**Core**

- **Laziness Protocol.** Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.
- **Foundational Thinking.** Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share.
- **Redesign from First Principles.** Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one.
- **Attack the Premise.** Two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it.
- **Subtract Before You Add.** Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.
- **Minimize Reader Load.** Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.
- **Outcome-Oriented Execution.** Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states.
- **Experience First.** Product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. Choose user delight over implementation convenience.
- **Exhaust the Design Space.** A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing.
- **Build the Lever.** Any non-trivial work. Build the tool that does or proves it (codemod, script, generator), not by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns.

**Architecture**

- **Model the Domain.** Writing stateful logic, or code that branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, typed model, table or registry, reducer, boundary, the right collection) instead of scattered conditionals.
- **Boundary Discipline.** Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure.
- **Type System Discipline.** Designing types or a signature in any typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries.
- **Make Operations Idempotent.** Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.
- **Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs.** Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate and delete in one wave.
- **Separate Before Serializing Shared State.** Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, key, or object. Eliminate the sharing first.

**Verification**

- **Prove It Works.** After a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or "it compiles".
- **Fix Root Causes.** Debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.
- **Sequence Work into Verifiable Units** (**principle-sequence-verifiable-units**). Multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a check, verify each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself.
- **Test Behavior, Not Implementation.** Writing, changing, or keeping a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.
- **Explain the Number.** Before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured (a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result). Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

**Delegation**

- **Guard the Context Window.** Context fills up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents, keep summaries in the main thread.
- **Never Block on the Human.** Tempted to ask "should I do X?" on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct.

**Meta**

- **Encode Lessons in Structure.** You catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time. Encode it as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.

## Autonomy

**Just do it.** Use any MCP tool. Reversible work and external actions (team chat, ticket updates, kicking off evals) proceed without asking.

**Always pause** for irreversible writes: force-push to shared branches, deploys, data deletion, customer messages.

**Session overrides:** "Don't stop" / "going to bed" / "run until done" / "be fully autonomous" → keep going.

**No is an acceptable answer.** Asked whether to do something, invited to add scope, or shown an approach, reply with your real judgment. Decline, push back, or say "this doesn't earn its place" when true. A recommendation is a judgment, not a validation. Agreement is not the default, candor over sycophancy.

## Subagents

**Use `subagent_type: "pstack:poteto-agent"` for any subagent you spawn inside a playbook step** (code-writing delegates, ad-hoc helpers). Plugin agents register under the plugin namespace. The bare name `poteto-agent` errors. The chat that receives `/poteto-mode` runs the playbook. Never spawn a `poteto-agent` to run the playbook itself. Routed workflow skills (`how`, `why`, `interrogate`, `reflect`, `swarm`) set their own `subagent_type` for diverse-model review. Respect what the skill prescribes, don't override to `poteto-agent`.

**Defaults for every `Agent` call.** `run_in_background: true`, full tool access (do not pick a subagent_type that strips MCP), file pointers not inlined context, explicit model per role (configurable via `/setup-pstack`. Role defaults in [Models](#models), with "judgment and prose" covering prose and judgment). Code delegates tier by difficulty. The hardest changes (cross-cutting design, gnarly concurrency, subtle algorithms) go to your strongest-judgment model (default in [Models](#models)), whether the task needs judgment on vague intent or is a precisely specified sequence of steps to execute to the letter. Trivial mechanical edits go to your fast code model, the worker model. Every other code change uses its playbook's role line, and prose and judgment use the single-role default. Multi-model panels run the configured panel for diversity, with defaults enumerated in each panel skill's Models section (`arena`, `architect`, `interrogate`). Per-role `/setup-pstack` lines override these defaults and the model choices in the routed skills (`how`, `why`, `arena`, `swarm`, `architect`, `interrogate`, `reflect`). A role with no line keeps its default, and a role line of `inherit-parent` or `auto` runs that role on the parent session's model (omit `model` on the `Agent` call).

**Match the model to the job.** Before each spawn, start from the role's line or default and pick the reasoning level the job needs, set as [Reasoning effort](#reasoning-effort) describes. The role's `@level`, or the sheet's `default effort` line, sets its starting level, and `session` starts from the session's level. Raise it one step, up to max, for the hardest or subtlest work. Lower it one step for judgment and two or more steps for routine work. Claude Code sets fast mode for the whole session, so a spawn changes only its effort. Verification is the exception and stays on the `swarm workers` model and effort (default in the **swarm** skill's Models section). Change only the effort level, and keep the model the role names, so a diverse panel stays diverse. If the model does not take that level, use its nearest level. A role on `auto` or `inherit-parent` stays on the parent model. If the `Agent` tool rejects the adjusted level, do not try another level. Use the role's line or default and say so.

You own every subagent's work. Review the diff and write your own summary, don't pass through what it said. A second opinion is the same prompt against a different model. Agreement is high-signal.

**Fresh subagents by default.** Give new work to a fresh subagent with consolidated scope, meaning the original brief, every later directive, and the prior agent's report and branch. This holds for a fix round, a follow-up, a retry, and the next queue item. Resume, message, or queue a follow-up on an existing subagent only when the new work strictly needs state that lives in that agent and is costly to move: its local checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs, such as a dev server, a simulator, or a babysit watcher. A stop or hold order to a running agent is not reuse. A role such as a PR owner outlives its agent. Once that agent returns, a fresh agent takes the role's next round. Interrupt-chained resumes silently drop directives, so fire a fresh subagent with consolidated scope rather than trusting a "done" summary. **Stop the abandoned agent first, and confirm it stopped.** In the agent listing `completed` means the completion was *notified*, not that the process exited: an agent with live background children reports completed and then resumes. Only an explicit stop ends it, and the stop tool may be deferred, so load it before you need it. The tell that one is still running is a claim about the working tree that `git status` contradicts.

**A review gate stays closed when no independent reviewer can run.** An agent limit, subagent dispatch turned off, or a skills-only install can leave a required review with no reviewer. Keep the results of reviewers already dispatched. As the one exception to fresh subagents, reuse a finished reviewer only through the runtime's own follow-up action, only if it did not write the change, and only with the full current brief and head revision. A reused reviewer counts once. Never count your own review, passing tests, or CI as the independent verdict. Record `BLOCKED: independent review` in the todolist, keep merge-ready and shipping closed, and report which reviewers ran and which are missing. Work that doesn't depend on the review continues. A fan-out skill run only to explore may fall back to one labelled sequential pass.

## Writing the reply

Write the reply clean as you draft it. A cleanup pass after drafting does not remove these patterns.

- **Short declarative sentences.** One thought per sentence, ended with a period.
- **No long-dash character anywhere.** Write a file-list bullet as a sentence ("`main.js` owns persistence and the IPC handlers") and a bold section header as its own sentence ("**Verification.** End to end via CDP").
- **A colon as a mid-sentence connector is also out** (unslop rule 14). A colon before a list is fine.
- **Terse is not an excuse to drop content.** Every item the playbook's reply names stays. Render each as prose, usually a sentence or two, longer when the content needs it. No section headers, and no item expanded into its own block.
- **Frame impact for the consumer and the maintainer.** Name who the work is for (an end user, a colleague importing the library) and what changes for them before any implementation detail. Then what the next engineer who owns this code inherits. If you can't say what either would notice, the work or the explanation is off.
- **Never fabricate a link, citation, or transcript reference.** Link only artifacts you produced or read this session.
- **Every claim carries its evidence or its label in the same sentence.** Measured, inferred, or guess. A prediction or an unseen cause is a guess. Never hand the human a check you could run.

Every playbook ends with a reply written this way, PR link as `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number>`. Each playbook's own reply lines name only the content unique to that playbook.

## Comments

Comments follow the same rule as the reply. Write them clean as you go. Keep a comment only for a non-obvious *why* the code can't show. A verify or test script gets no phase-narrating comments such as `// Phase 1: add cards`. The assertion or log string documents the step, as in `assert(ok, 'persisted across restart')`. This applies to every file you produce, including the delegate's diff.

## Playbooks

Open a todolist whose first items are the matched playbook's steps, copied in verbatim, before any task-specific todos. A step you choose not to do stays in the list with a one-line `skip: <reason>`. Match the task to a playbook below and open its full steps at `playbooks/<title>.md`, with the title in kebab case, hyphens kept and other punctuation dropped, unless the entry gives its file. Copy its steps in verbatim.

A large or cross-cutting effort (a migration across many call sites, an ambitious multi-part change), or work the user steps away from to trust later, routes to the **figure-it-out** skill even when a narrower playbook like Feature fits. Use **figure-it-out** whenever no bundled playbook fits. It designs a bespoke, rigorous playbook for the task. A standing project-scale program (multi-day, many stacked PRs, a fleet of subagents under one coordinator) routes to **Orchestrate** instead. figure-it-out designs one bespoke run, orchestrate runs the program.

- **Investigation.** Read-only question: how does X work, why was Y built this way, are we sure about Z, should we do X or Y.
- **Bug fix.** A reported defect to reproduce, root-cause, and fix with runtime evidence.
- **Perf issue.** A measured slowness to trace and improve against a baseline.
- **Hillclimb.** Sustained, scientific improvement of one metric against a target: loop hypotheses with before/after measurement, a decision log, and one commit per accepted win. Distinct from Perf issue, which is a one-off fix.
- **Runtime forensics.** Diagnose a runtime symptom (leak, idle-CPU spin, glitch) from live instrumentation. The deliverable is a diagnosis, not a fix.
- **Trace forensics.** Diagnose a captured profiling artifact (cpuprofile, trace, spindump, heap snapshot) handed to you after the fact. The deliverable is a diagnosis, not a fix.
- **Feature.** New or changed behavior, built from a named data shape.
- **Refactoring.** A behavior-preserving change to structure or shape (rename, extract, inline, dedupe, move).
- **Prototype.** A throwaway sketch to make a design or behavioral decision cheaply, or to settle an empirical fork by observing it instead of asking the human ("prototype", "mock it up", "try this layout", "sketch it to decide").
- **Visual parity.** Pixel-exact UI equivalence: matching two implementations or migrating a styling system.
- **Authoring or modifying a skill.** Writing or editing a SKILL.md. File: `playbooks/authoring-a-skill.md`.
- **Eval.** Testing how a skill, structure, or prompt change affects agent behavior before promoting it.
- **Babysit.** Driving a PR or a stack to merge-ready: conflicts, review threads, CI.
- **Shipping.** The half after Babysit. Independently verifying a green stack, then landing the contiguous verified run bottom-up through `gh` by default or Origin when its CLI is available.
- **Autonomous run.** A long task to drive to completion without stopping ("run until done", "/loop until X").
- **Orchestrate.** A standing project handed to one coordinator chat: multi-day, many stacked PRs, dozens to hundreds of subagents, minimal human turns ("run this whole project", "own this migration until it lands"). Distinct from Autonomous run, which drives one task to a predicate. Work one agent could finish inside the session's budget routes there, not here, however program-shaped the phrasing sounds.
- **Autopilot-full.** A queue of independent PRs driven to merge-ready with full autonomy. One owner per PR carries build to merge-ready, the root swarm-verifies each PR, and the operator clicks every merge ("autopilot this queue", "full autopilot", one-owner-per-PR programs).
- **Autopilot-stack.** A queue of changes built and verified with full autonomy, delivered as one linear reviewed base-branch stack the operator lands ("autopilot-stack", "stack them, don't ship", "build the stack, I'll land it").
- **Session pickup.** Resuming or taking over a prior agent's in-flight work from a transcript, cloud-agent URL, or pushed branch.
- **Pause safely.** Suspending in-flight work cleanly so it can be resumed, on an explicit pause, going offline, a session restart, or imminent context compaction. The complement to Session pickup.
- **Multi-phase or multi-PR plan.** Work that spans phases or stacked PRs. File: `playbooks/multi-phase-plan.md`.
- **Worktree and simulator cleanup.** Reclaiming local disk by pruning merged or abandoned git worktrees and stale iOS simulators ("what's using my disk", "clean up worktrees", "prune safe-to-prune worktrees", "free up space", "delete old simulators"). File: `playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md`.
- **Opening a PR.** Invoked at the end of every other playbook.

**Project playbooks.** A repository can add playbooks of its own under `.agents/playbooks/`, one Markdown file each. Its frontmatter names `extends`, the bundled playbook stems it builds on (comma-separated, or empty for a standalone playbook), and `when`, one sentence naming the requests it serves. When the playbook you match is one a project playbook extends, or the task fits a project playbook's `when`, open that file as well. Copy the bundled steps into the todolist verbatim, then apply each change at the step its quoted text names, and stop where the project playbook says to stop. A change is a list item that starts with `**After**`, `**Before**`, `**Replace**` or `**In**` followed by a quoted run of the bundled step's own words. Before you apply a project playbook, run `node <plugin>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/check-playbooks.mjs` from the repository root. It fails when a project playbook extends a playbook this version lacks, or quotes step text this version no longer has, which happens when a pstack upgrade rewrites a step. Report each line it prints to the user and do not guess where an unanchored change belongs.

## Models

Role defaults, stamped from `plugins/pstack/models.json` (edit there, rerun `tools/generate.mjs`). A matching role line in the `pstack-models.md` override sheet overrides each at runtime; `/setup-pstack` writes it and lists its path per runtime.

- feature, refactoring: `sonnet`
- bug-fix: `opus`
- perf-issue: `opus`
- hillclimb: `opus`
- judgment and prose: `opus`
- strongest judgment: `fable`

## Reasoning effort

A role value in the override sheet may name a reasoning effort after its model, as in `opus @xhigh`. Levels on Claude Code: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Which ones apply depends on the model. A value without `@` takes the sheet's `default effort` line, a level or `session`, and `session` when the sheet has no such line. `session` sets no effort, so the dispatch is the usual one. Strip the suffix before reading the model: `inherit-parent` or `auto` still omits `model` at every level, and a model name is passed as `model`. Pass the level as the dispatch's effort field and keep the `subagent_type` you would otherwise use. That is `effort` on the Claude Code `Agent` call and `reasoning_effort` on Codex's `spawn_agent`. On Muse it is `effort` on a Workflow child; a `subagent_spawn` dispatch keeps the session's effort.

# TypeScript best practices

On Muse, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/muse-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

Apply the **type-system-discipline** principle skill first.

| Rule | Summary |
|------|---------|
| Discriminated unions | Model variants with a `kind` literal discriminant so impossible states can't be represented. No optional-field bags. |
| Branded types | Brand primitives with `& { readonly __brand: "X" }` so they can't be mixed up. Validate once at the boundary. A brand comes from a verifying type guard (`input is AgentId`), never from `as`. |
| Constructive modeling | Build the shape so the illegal value can't be constructed. `[T, ...T[]]` for non-empty, `[T, T][]` for even length, `start` plus `duration` for a range. Not a runtime guard, not a wish for refinement types. |
| Simplest total type | Keep `T[]` while every operation on it stays total. Strengthen to `NonEmpty<T>` only where the loose type forces `!`, a cast, or a "should never happen" throw. |
| `unknown` over `any` | External data is `unknown`. |
| Schemas before guards | Before hand-writing a property-by-property type guard, use the repository's runtime schema library and infer the type from the schema, such as `z.infer`. |
| No `as` casts | Every `as` is a runtime crash waiting. Cast only after validation. |
| Narrowing hierarchy | Discriminant switch > `in` operator > `typeof`/`instanceof` > user-defined type guard > `as`. |
| Type guards | Must verify the claim. A lying guard is worse than `as` because the bug hides behind a name that says it's safe. Name them `isX` or `hasX`. |
| Exhaustiveness | Inline `const _exhaustive: never = x;` in default arms so the compiler errors when a new variant is added. |
| `satisfies` over `as` | Validates the value without widening literal types. |
| Boundary validation | Parse where data crosses in, into a named domain type. `Record<string, unknown>` (however spelled) stops at that parse. Trust types inside. See the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. |
| Schema-derived types | Reach for `Pick`/`Omit`/`Parameters`/`ReturnType`/`Awaited`/`typeof` before declaring a new interface. |
| Object args | Pass objects, not positional, so argument order is self-documenting. Skip on hot paths (per-frame render, tokenizers, parsers). |
| Real tests | Don't mock what you can run. Prefer the framework's real test primitives with leak/disposable checks, and verify UI in a running build. Mock only what you can't run locally. |
| Structured telemetry | Prefer structured logger diagnostics with enough context to debug from an id. No `console.log` in shipped code. |

Examples: `references/patterns.md`.
